results.content: This brief examines how Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds LLMs in real knowledge to reduce hallucinations. To make AI reliable for enterprise use, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a leading solution. RAG combines retrieval with generation, grounding responses in real data rather than model memory (Vaderav, 2025). Since enterprises change often, RAG ensures AI stays current by updating the data source instead of retraining the model (Gupta et al., 2024). RAG addresses key causes of hallucination by supplying missing knowledge and enabling output verification against retrieved sources. RAG grounds its outputs in trusted sources, such as company documents or knowledge graphs, thereby reducing hallucinations (Gupta et al., 2024). * RAG can retrieve real-time data from databases or APIs, enabling AI to provide up-to-date answers. Enterprises are now building retrieval layers (e.g., vector indexes, knowledge graphs, and APIs) as the foundation for reliable, RAG-based systems. Agentic RAG lets AI decide when to retrieve data or use tools, enabling more complex, fact-based reasoning (Vaderav, 2025).

results.title: Reducing LLM Hallucinations: A Developer's Guide - Zep
results.content: | **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** | Incorporates real-time external data retrieval into model prompts, significantly reducing hallucinations by grounding responses in factual data. * **Reduced Knowledge Gaps**: RAG helps when the model "doesn't know what it doesn't know." If the answer isn't in the model's parameters but exists in the external data, the retrieval step can fill in that gap and prevent a hallucinated guess . A fine-tuned model is less likely to hallucinate because it has essentially "learned" from examples what information is correct and what it should do when it's unsure. Developers have an expanding toolbox: **better prompts, curated data, retrieval augmentation, long-term memory, and even model fine-tuning** for factual correctness. For example, you might use RAG for grounding on top of a model that was fine-tuned on your domain, and also employ prompt tricks like chain-of-thought, then add a final layer of verification for critical outputs.
